statements.text:
America’s national security must always come first.

Today, I’m proud to announce my priorities for strengthening our national defense, supporting our service members and veterans, and protecting Tennessee’s military communities.

As your Congressman, I will work to:

Maintain a strong, well-equipped military ready to defend our nation.
Secure our borders and protect America from foreign threats.
Keep America ahead in artificial intelligence and critical technology.
Ensure service members, military families, and veterans receive the care and support they deserve.
Improve military housing and quality of life while protecting Tennessee’s military installations.
End DEI-based military policies and put merit, readiness, and mission requirements first.
Expand education, training, and career opportunities for those who serve.
Protect America’s food supply, energy, water, and other critical resources.
Stand up for Tennessee’s veterans with a 100% disability rating and protect their earned benefits.

From Fort Campbell to Naval Support Activity Mid-South, I will stand with Tennessee’s military communities and fight for the resources our armed forces need to defend our nation.

Those who defend our freedom deserve a Congressman who will fight for them.

Strong defense. Strong Tennessee. Strong America.
I don’t like data centers or even solar panels on productive land, farmland. If you know anything about me, I’m a land preservationist.
statements.venue: Interview with The Tennessee Journal (State Affairs) at campaign headquarters launch

statements.text:
This should be a local decision and data centers should be put in places that make sense; however, this is also a national security issue. We cannot let China win the AI race.

Technology and data centers can bring investment and economic development to Tennessee, but local families and small businesses should not be stuck paying the bill for someone else’s expansion. Large data center operators should be responsible for the additional infrastructure and electricity costs directly attributable to their operations, rather than passing those costs along to residential customers.
statements.venue: Main Street Media of Tennessee candidate Q&A
